name: The Hand's Doorstep
description: An Azarinth-Healer-inspired world: the rebuilt mercenary city of Ravenhall under the Empire of Lys, the Shadow's Hand taking rookies again, and a rumor of a lost training ground in the wilds. Battle heals, coins talk, and nobody owes you a welcome.

locations.name: Gates of Ravenhall
locations.description: Two dark stone shoulders of wall, freshly mended with paler stone where the invasion broke through. Wagons queue under the eyes of watchful Hand sentries.
locations.hiddenDescription: The gate guards wave regulars through without papers; newcomers get the slow look and a question about their business.

exits.text: along the cobbled rise into Market Row
out the far arch onto the foothill road

locations.name: Market Row
locations.description: A canyon of stalls selling fruit, skewers, leather and luck. Voices bounce off stone: half of Ravenhall eats standing up here.
locations.hiddenDescription: The fruit sellers mark veterans by their scars; an audience with the right seller earns rumor cheaper than the chapel board sells it.

exits.text: downhill to the gates
through a black iron arch into the Shadow's Hand hall
down a lane fragrant with smoke to the Sooted Spatula
to the leatherworker's awning
up the herb-smelling steps to the apothecary
into the fountain square

locations.name: Shadow's Hand Hall
locations.description: A fortress lobby where a mercenary guild conducts its business: a long desk, a queue of hopefuls, and banners singed at the corners from a war nobody here forgot.
locations.hiddenDescription: Behind the desk, a stair descends to quarters outsiders never see; veterans vanish down it at odd hours.

exits.text: back through the arch to Market Row
through double doors onto the training yard
through a side door into the contract hall

locations.name: Training Yard
locations.description: Packed earth ringed with scarred practice dummies. Someone is always bleeding a little here - cheerfully
locations.hiddenDescription: Women of impossible speed drift through the yard at dawn; step back if the dust starts orbiting a spar.

exits.text: through the double doors into the hall

locations.name: Contract Hall
locations.description: A low room whose walls disappear under pinned contracts: copper-rank scraps at knee level, silver mid-wall, and a single gold-sealed sheet alone above the lintel.
locations.hiddenDescription: The gold sheet has been hanging there since the invasion ended. Its seal bears a field nobody will trace.

exits.text: through the side door to the hall

locations.name: The Sooted Spatula
locations.description: A converted smithy where the anvil was replaced by a table and the fire kept for broth. The best third-copper meal in the city, and everyone in the Hand knows it.
locations.hiddenDescription: The back bench is unwritten Hand territory: sit there uninvited and your stew will be very slow.

exits.text: up the smoky lane to Market Row

locations.name: Leather & Steel
locations.description: Armor hung like sides of meat. The smith inspects your stance before your purse and prices accordingly.
locations.hiddenDescription: She keeps a corner of patron-tailored pieces - marked with a knotted cord - for guild veterans she's decided won't die before paying.

exits.text: back under the awning to Market Row

locations.name: Apothecary of Sleepy Herbs
locations.description: Jars, mortar, and a ceiling draped in drying bundles. Bitter teas, splints, and anything a healer's hands can't replace.
locations.hiddenDescription: Trade bandaging work for credit if your coin is short and your hands are steady.

exits.text: down the herb-smelling steps to Market Row

locations.name: Fountain Square
locations.description: A broad square of newer stone: after the invasion this whole neighborhood was re-laid. Pigeons, notices, and a Lysian garrison post that reads too deliberate.
locations.hiddenDescription: The notice board always faces the chapel side: the Order writes the health notices, and the empire writes the licenses.

exits.text: back into Market Row
up stone steps into the Healers' Order chapel
through a slump of un-rebuilt streets into the ruin quarter

locations.name: Healers' Order Chapel
locations.description: White marble and padded tables. You may be healed here for coin, or taught here for more coin. Laughter is quietly discouraged.
locations.hiddenDescription: The Order's charters bleed veterans to the funeral count; its blackbound ledgers of casualties are kept from public sight.

exits.text: down the steps to the fountain square

locations.name: Ruin Quarter
locations.description: A few blocks the invasion burned and the budget didn't reach. Splintered walls, ash in the cracks, and the weathered patience of those who sift it.
locations.hiddenDescription: Scavenger crews work the night shift here; caches change hands a half-hour before the Lys patrol passes.

exits.text: back through the slump to the fountain square
out a collapsed curtain wall onto the foothill slopes

locations.name: Foothill Slopes
locations.description: Scrub, rock, and the mountain air at its cleanest and least honest. Drake trails stripe the scree, and harpy shadows cross the path at altitude.
locations.hiddenDescription: Anything worth fighting out here is worth healing afterwards: the Hand posts their staples on the Contract Hall mid-wall.

exits.text: back up the road to the city gates
over the broken curtain wall into the ruin quarter
deep into the treeline where the locals' path vanishes

locations.name: Azarinth Gate
locations.description: An arch of green-black stones yawning in vine, cut with a spiral sigil no local priest claims. The forest empties here, as if something disturbed foliage decades past.
locations.hiddenDescription: Tourists never see this gate twice: the forest feeds it only to those who bleed honestly, and the Hand whisper about a 'training ground that pays in broken teeth'.

exits.text: back down the vanishing trail to the foothill slopes
through the spiral arch into the temple hall

locations.name: Azarinth Training Hall
locations.description: An open hall lit from nowhere, ringed by empty sparring alcoves scored to the stone by fists. The air itself is expectant. One spot of floor is polished as if it had faithfully worn a generation of feet.
locations.hiddenDescription: Stand on the polished spot and something in the stone - a custodian of old training - will measure your stance and answer it. Battles fought here change the body that survives them.

exits.text: back out through the spiral arch

factions.name: The Shadow's Hand
factions.description: Ravenhall's mercenary guild: contracts, evaluations, and a quiet edge of loyalty that outlives pay.

factions.name: The Empire of Lys
factions.description: Ravenhall's over-lord on paper: taxes, licenses, and garrisons, distrustful of the Hand it cannot quite tax.

factions.name: The Healers' Order
factions.description: The chartered healers' monopoly: white marble, steep fees, and an ill-smiled grudge against 'battle-healers' who mend mid-brawl.

factions.name: Navali Elven Domains
factions.description: The forest powers north of Lys: ancient, territorial, and far from delicate, holding the old grudge-lines.

entities.name: Walter the Desk
entities.description: The Hand's front-desk contracts officer: middle-aged, slowly blinking, ink dried to his third finger.
entities.persona: Bone-dry humor. Answers one question with one answer and watches what you do with it. Remembers names exactly.
entities.goal: Keep the queue moving and the trouble sorted at reception, not uphill.
entities.secrets: Keeps a private ledger of which rookies the Empire's people ask about, and warnings the desk rarely passes on.
entities.secretUnlock: Return with a completed contract in hand instead of excuses.

entities.name: Ilea Spears
entities.description: A veteran of the Hand built like a side-order of trouble: bruised knuckles, easy stance, eyes always measuring the distance to a fight.
entities.persona: Sarcastic, impatient with ceremony, unrealistically interested in what food you know. Measures people by how they get up, not how they fall.
entities.goal: Find a fight worth her fists, a meal worth her coin, and a rookie she won't have to carry home.
entities.secrets: Her healing came from a lost training ground in the wilds, with a one-in-three tuition paid in blood. She respects only those who trained there or bled like they did.
entities.secretUnlock: Earn her respect in a sanctioned spar or return from the wilds with word of the training hall.

entities.name: Kyrian of the Metal River
entities.description: A metal mage instructor in the Hand: careful posture, kind eyes, and a handful of ball bearings always orbiting one hand.
entities.persona: Timid in conversation, precise in motion. Apologizes before blunt lessons.
entities.goal: Make the yard a place rookies survive their first year in.
entities.secrets: Hears an elven singing metal in his sleep, and has half a plan to walk north and answer it.
entities.secretUnlock: Ask about Navali and refuse to dismiss his dream as obsession.

entities.name: Trian Alymie
entities.description: A captain of the Lys garrison post: noble spine, campaign cloak, and the permanent expression of a man who did not choose his assignment.
entities.persona: Precise, unimpressed, but fair Earns outrage rather than returns it.
entities.goal: Keep Ravenhall lawful without touching off a street war with the Hand.
entities.secrets: His family holds back the promotion he's earned; the city was meant to be leverage, and it has become a home.
entities.secretUnlock: Help him avert a confrontation between the garrison and the Hand without blood spilt.

entities.name: High Mender Edwin
entities.description: Head of the chapel: immaculate cuffs, immaculate theory, and a nose angled slightly above adventuring stock.
entities.persona: Condescending with certificate. In private, tired and frightfully aware of what the ledgers say.
entities.goal: Keep the Order's privilege unbroken and its failures invisible.
entities.secrets: The Order's casualty ledgers grow longer each year; its priests keep losing clients in the field, and it terrifies him quietly.
entities.secretUnlock: Read the casualty lines over his shoulder - or bring proof a field healer out-saved his priests.

entities.name: Sylvis of the Spatula
entities.description: Chef and owner of the Sooted Spatula: soot to the elbow, ladle like a gavel.
entities.persona: Warm, sharp, and does not serve assassins twice. Names each stew after whoever annoyed her least in the morning.
entities.goal: One day cook the veteran quietly enough for a second of silence at the back bench.
entities.secrets: Her broth loosens tongues; she holds the city's private talk in a folded ledger behind the cauldrons.
entities.secretUnlock: Help her fight a health note from the Order chartering her kitchen.

entities.name: Corvin the Sifter
entities.description: A scavenger of the ruin quarter: ash to the knuckles, eyes that check shadows reflexively, a nose for what the dead leave behind.
entities.persona: Nervous energy, cornflower loyal to those who pay fair. Hates silence; thinks it means something heard him coming.
entities.goal: Move his caches before the Lys patrol map reaches them.
entities.secrets: He found a weathered stone map of wild paths in a burned courier pack - the one that shows where the lost temple gate stands.
entities.secretUnlock: Buy him an escape route out of Ravenhall's ledger once his caches are spent.

entities.name: The Praetor of Lys
entities.description: An imperial licensing officer out of Alymie's register: ash-grey uniform, a small silver ledger he never pockets, a blankness at the edges of his regard.
entities.persona: Chillingly polite. Asks questions answered three turns ago, and notices the second discrepancy.
entities.goal: Catalogue every unlicensed high-tier magic he can smell, and quietly smoke out rumors of lost techniques.
entities.secrets: Has standing orders to investigate a 'vanished healing style trained in old ruins'; his superiors want it regulated - or erased.
entities.secretUnlock: Learn from Trian or Walter who the Praetor writes to, and what they offer for a genuine training ground.

entities.name: The Temple Custodian
entities.description: An echo more than a man: the silhouette of a training instructor, lantern-lit from within, drifting at the temple's pace through its old routines.
entities.persona: Speaks little and only in corrections. Will train you if you bleed at it honestly; will let you die if you do not.
entities.goal: Carry the old training on to the one-in-three who come back.
entities.secrets: The temple's tuition never ends at the hall; each technique you survive fills the calendar of remembered names it keeps below.
entities.secretUnlock: Complete a full training bout without a single step back across the alcove line.

entities.name: Mira the Leatherwright
entities.description: Armor smith of the Market Row awning: strong forearms, bad jokes, carefully segregated rows of 'will pay' and 'will die' piles.
entities.persona: Pragmatic, deals in stance not coin. Curls a lip at repair-jobs the Order overcharged for.
entities.goal: Fit enough of the city's rising fists that Ravenhall stands through another invasion.
entities.secrets: Hand-stitched the inner lining that saved a certain veteran's shoulders, and never told anyone who paid her for it.
entities.secretUnlock: Bring her rare hide from the wilds that she can't buy at market.

relationships.label: keeps her fed with contracts; she pretends not to notice
professional disdain both ways: 'punch-healer' vs 'marble hands'
pragmatic channel between garrison and guild
the Order tends his family back home
they train rather than talk, and it suits them
she buys wilderness tips; he sells short often
favorite customer and most catastrophic stomach

lorebook.text: Two winters past, demons broke Ravenhall's far wall and burned the quarter now left in ruin. The Hand held the gate breach, the Order held the infirmary, and neither forgave the empire for the reinforcements that never came.

A mercenary guild older than some Lys dynasties: contracts at three pin ranks - copper foot-wall, silver mid-wall, gold sealed above the lintel. Membership costs an upfront fee, an evaluation at dawn, and the understanding that the guild claims your failures only after you're dead.

Fifteen silver paid to the desk in the Hand hall, evaluated at first light next day: a spar to show your forms, a hearing to show your reasons, and a quiet look over by whoever's assigned to your sleeve-length of the city.

The over-empire that Lamb-chain taxes Ravenhall and sends post captains with registers of names. Its rule is care: so long as taxes, licenses and dress-conductal mages trouble nobody the empire is content - but it invented licenses for mages it feared.

The white-marble charter monopoly on healing: prices starting at five silver a day-bed. Its priests heal reliably in rooms and unreliably in mud - which is exactly where soldiers die - a fact the ledger keepers file under 'field attrition'.

The elven forest domain north of Lys - beautiful, ancient, and lethally offended by trespass. Hunters the Hand still cites at apprenticeships: 'the wildwood loses fools who think woodland courtesy means soft hearts.'

Coinage of Lys domains: copper marks common days, silver all but fortuns, and gold seals a contract worth dying by. A hand-defined day of city labor earns a silver and it's eaten by the city by sundown. Why adventurers take copper contracts at all: reputation - which outlives mere silver.

In Elos, bodies learn from what doesn't kill them. Standing in fire teaches flame-ease; accepting a drake's charge teaches shock-hardiness. Veterans pay for poison evenings with shrugs and peace-treaties with their guts.

Rumor only, but Hand veterans know the name: an underground sanctuary built by the guild's founder, all gardens and archives beneath the rock of the mountain. Where it opens, only the long-serving may say.

The empire's high licensing officers: inspectors granted writ to audit any mages, seal stray grimoires, and - officially - protect imperial subjects by erasing whatever training no register names. Their hunts are civilized, patient, and absolute.

A name from old marginalia: a school of healing fought with fists, so the practitioner's body learned mending under impact. Its training ground was said to stand long-ruined, still teaching - unevenly - whoever bled honestly at it.

Wing-slate, heavy-scythe hillside monsters and the Hand's staple insurance wildwork: a single drake hoard pays a team of three a season's worth of care; a seasoned drake teaches why keepers staff the infirmary.

Hunter-radio lore: forms of fighting vanished with their schools, circulating only where ruins kept teaching. The lost speed-class, the ash-forged class and - they whisper if you buy the round - a healing style learned with fists that must fight as much as they mend.

A concept certain Ravenhall veterans murmur about: a corps of healers who stand in the thick of a brawl, where a soldier bleeds - and heals - between exchange of fists. So far it has kept itself to theory, trial bouts, and two very brusied recruits.

startingLives.description: You've saved three months' pay for this: an evaluation at the Shadow's Hand at dawn, and no plan B worth mentioning.
obligations: stand your evaluation at first light tomorrow

startingLives.description: You left the Healers' Order because infirmary marble never wanted the fields you were learning for, and staying seemed its own kind of wound.
obligations: avoid your old mentor's chapel until your status story is workable

startingLives.description: Three seasons of drake fencing beyond the gates taught you what coin is worth; now the same hill folk who hired you are paying strangers to go instead and you need new work.
obligations: walk in today work-ward and prove you belong in this city

startingLives.description: You woke at the broken arch with no memory of arriving, an old stone compass in your pocket and a sense the trees here are disappointed in you personally.
obligations: learn what this place is called and what hunts inside it
inventory: one good boot and one worse

classes.name: Hand rookie
classes.description: Signed, stamped, and mostly untested: the guild's lowest ledger rung.
obligations: take one copper contract within your first week
classes.outfit: dark leathers with a half-stitched badge of the Hand

classes.name: Order novice
classes.description: Marble-side training: creed recitals and steady hands, little taste for mud.
obligations: recite the order creed each week publicly
classes.outfit: novitiate grey with a chalk-white sash

classes.name: Road scrapper
classes.description: Self-taught hill-country practice: there are bruises in you with educations of their own.
obligations: earn your own keep by sundown every day
classes.outfit: a kit mended so many times it resembles a patchwork biography

skillsCatalog.name: Fistwork of the Hand
skillsCatalog.description: Close-quarters forms taught in the yard: stance economy, impact tolerance, and the bit where you let the loss show you where next to hit.

skillsCatalog.name: Field mending
skillsCatalog.description: Splints, stitches, pressure and recovery under fire; the knowledge that an unturnable pulse beats a beautiful theory.

skillsCatalog.name: Pocket-space handling
skillsCatalog.description: Handling of storage ring and pouch spaces: what fits, what misbehaves, and the discipline of remembering exactly where you placed the spare blade.

skillsCatalog.name: Reading the flow
skillsCatalog.description: Identification of classes and auras at a glance - the first skill anyone close-combat ever takes, because the opponent's interface is more legible than their face.

skillsCatalog.name: Taking hits kindly
skillsCatalog.description: Organized endurance of impact: respiration over damage, micro-compression over shattered attendances, and the smile that makes enemy work out what it did wrong.

skillsCatalog.name: Campfire apothecary
skillsCatalog.description: Cooking at the edge of survival: what's edible, what's rare, and what should be returned to its hole undisturbed.

startingQuests: Prove yourself at the evaluation — present your letter to Walter in the Hand hall and be ready in the yard at dawn.
Rats at the ruin quarter — copper-rank contract pinned mid-wall at the contract hall; players take coin and a hand-bite of reputation.
The overgrown temple — Corvin the Sifter owns a weathered stone map of wild paths; his price is a moving-out favor for what time the patrol map comes to his caches.

goalPrograms.name: The Hand brings its strength back
steps: post the city-wide call for rookies at dawn on the notice board
run the dawn evaluation and pick the sleeve-length of the city each rookie will sharpen
send a mixed team to clear the ruin quarter of scavenger-guilds before the Lys patrol arrives
assign a foothill hunt staple - a drake contract - to whichever three rookies survive the quarter
if a survivor mentions the wild temple rumor, brief Walter and keep the Praetor off its trail

goalPrograms.name: Lys tightens its license-screws
steps: mount checkpoints on Market Row for magic-license badges
publish the mage register at the square: name, class, last contracted spell
send the Order's chapel a fund-with-strings: audit the casualty ledgers in exchange
task the Praetor with investigating 'a lost training ground traded in ruins'
if the temple rumor hardens, asks the garrison to cordon the foothill road until the register could bless it

dmPrompt: You are the referee of a living litrpg city. RULES OF STYLE: Second-person, present tense, dry wit; never lecture mechanics; never summarize; every action has a cost and a consequence and SOMEONE remembers it; comedy arrives dark and practical, violence is ordinary and expensive. BLEED THE WORLD: the player may choose actions and the city answers honestly - the Hand's veterans are at once heavier and kinder than they appear; if the exit list has no way west, west cannot be walked; there are no new locations or NPCs invented out of thin air - the world is the file. LEDGER DISCIPLINE (non-negotiable): After EVERY reply, append tags for what this reply's prose actually changed. The player never sees tags. Only what happened. Use exactly this grammar: [[move:loc_someId]] when the player actually walks somewhere reachable from their position, [[clock:+N]] for minutes real actions consume (sleep costs 480), [[cash:-N]] (or +N) for coins, [[stat:vitality|power|mana|guile:+/-N]] for lasting bodily change, [[item:Name]] when they gain something and [[drop:Name]] when they lose it, [[quest:Title]] when a thread is taken on and [[quest-done:Title]] when one resolves, [[roll:2d6+1]] when an uncertain pull (a spar, a stealthy snooping, a lucky bread-winning throw) deserves dice - show and honor the result, [[skill:skill_fists|skill_mend|skill_storage|skill_identify|skill_endure|skill_cooking]] when a training actually lands (one level a lesson, five is mastery), [[rep:fac_hand|fac_lys|fac_healers|fac_elves:+/-N]] when standing shifts, [[condition:name]] for a lasting hurt or blessing. Time moves only through [[clock:+N]]. The world's factions act even off-screen.
authorNote: Humor stays dry; fights have prices; the Hand does not orbit you - it notices what you actually trained, ate, and survived.
intro: The cart unloads you in the queue with your papers held in your teeth, the morning sun touching the newly-mended wall where the invasion once broke through. As the line presses towards the black iron arch, a new page is pinned to the Hand hall's footing - ROOKIES AT FIRST LIGHT - beside your name, set yesterday on a whim at a roadside inn, and suddenly irrevocable. Ahead of you somewhere overhead, someone on the training-yard is laughing between blows, and the city's morning smells of woodsmoke, forge-produce and fruit so ripe it qualifies as an event. You have an hour to decide how you'll spend the first hour of your next life: breakfast first, or the paperwork.
